notes: HEFSP filed BER-L-000798-25 on 06/30/2025 (129 pages). Planner: Burgis Associates. DCA obligation accepted in full: present need 81 units, prospective need 92 units. FSHC settlement in place. Borough intends to satisfy entirety of 92-unit Prospective Need. Table 25 components: 343 total units / 69 affordable + 23 bonus = 92 credits (bonus capped at 25% of obligation). 350 Mt. Pleasant Ave (Latex site) generates transit bonus for proximity to Wood Ridge Rail Station. Present Need (81 units) addressed via housing rehabilitation program. Third Round sites (Table 23) carried: Morningside Block 71 Lots 35.01 & 35.02; Wallington Homes Block 70.05 Lot 8.01; 4H Site Block 70.01 Lot 78 (18% set-aside, 269-275 total units).

sites.proposed_zoning: MAAH-1 Zone / Midland Avenue Affordable Housing Zone (inclusionary; 23.8 du/acre)
sites.quote: 1 Midland Avenue, Block 71, Lot 1. This 2.94 acre site is an old factory complex that is occupied by failing structures, debris and vehicle storage. ... It is the Borough's intention to rezone the parcel for inclusionary development for a total of 70 units of which 14 will be affordable to low and moderate income families.
sites.notes: Known contaminated site per NJDEP. Flood plain along easterly property line (Saddle River). Approximately 2.5 acres of buildable area. Borough also authorized Planning Board to investigate as area in need of redevelopment under LRHL. Zone identified as MAAH-1 in ordinance appendix. 14 credits / 0 bonus = 14 total credits (Table 25).

sites.quote: 2 & 34 Midland Avenue, Block 26.02, Lots 14 & 15. Located directly across the street from 1 Midland Avenue this is a 1.571 acre parcel that is occupied by a granite and tile company with outdoor storage secured by an 8-foot slatted fence that creates a visual block along the street. ... It is the Borough's intention to rezone the parcel for inclusionary development for a total of 35 units 7 of will be affordable to low and moderate income families.
sites.notes: Known contaminated site per NJDEP. Flood plain along westerly property line (Passaic River). At least 1.0 acres of buildable area. Borough intends to investigate as potential redevelopment area. 7 credits / 0 bonus = 7 total credits (Table 25).

sites.current_zoning: MAAH-2 Zone (Midland Avenue Affordable Housing Zone-2)
sites.quote: 95-99 Midland Avenue, Block 71, Lots 13-14. This is an 18 unit inclusionary multifamily development that will yield 4 affordable units. Resolution of approval is attached to the appendices.
sites.notes: Approved project per Table 25 (*). Resolution of approval included in appendix. Zone identified as MAAH-2 in ordinance appendix (Block 71 Lots 13-14). 4 credits / 0 bonus = 4 total credits.

sites.current_zoning: MUAH Zone (Mixed-Use Affordable Housing Zone proposed)
sites.quote: 434 Main Avenue (Bl 70.01/L 4.01): 70 total units, 14 affordable units, 0 bonus credits, 14 total credits, 3.50 acres, 21.4 du/acre.
sites.notes: Zone identified as MUAH (Mixed-Use Affordable Housing Zone) in ordinance appendix for Block 70.01 Lot 4.01. 14 credits / 0 bonus = 14 total credits (Table 25).

sites.quote: 67 Paterson Avenue, Block 28, Lot 13. The Borough approved a 10 unit townhouse development that will yield 2 affordable units. Resolution of approval is attached to the appendices.
sites.notes: Approved project per Table 25 (*). Table 25 also references Lots 13-15 for this site. Resolution of approval in appendix. Developer: 67 Paterson Avenue LLC. Applicant required to set aside 2 units restricted to eligible persons under NJ affordable housing regulations. 2 credits / 0 bonus = 2 total credits.

sites.proposed_zoning: Latex Redevelopment Zone — redevelopment plan to permit 140 units, no less than 20% affordable
sites.quote: 350 Mount Pleasant Avenue, Block 70.01, Lot 80. This a 9.67 acre site owned by the Borough of Wallington. The property has been remediated to a residential standard from its earlier condition of contamination and has been designated an area in need of redevelopment by the Borough. As a redevelopment site nearly abutting the Wood Ridge Rail Station, the site is ideally suited to inclusionary development. It is the intention of the Borough to adopt a redevelopment plan to permit the development of 140 units of which 28 units will be designated for low and moderate income families.
sites.notes: Borough-owned. Remediated to residential standard. Designated area in need of redevelopment (Resolution 2023-76). Redevelopment plan adopted for LRAZ. Transit bonus: within 1/2 mile of Wood Ridge Rail Station — generates 23 bonus credits (capped at 25% of 92-unit obligation). 28 affordable + 23 bonus = 51 total credits (Table 25). Redevelopment plan appendix also identifies Block 70, Lots 1.01, 404 and 80 / Block 70.01 Lots 2, 80, 1.01, 1.02, 4.02, 4.03, 4.04 in expanded study area.
